subject: Tenant orthogonalization — cost & latency workflow
messages:
From: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>
To: Observability Product Team <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Observability Eng <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Platform Eng Lead <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Acme Analytics <amanda@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant orthogonalization — cost & latency workflow

Team,

Quick note to surface an ask from Acme (cc'd) that I think maps to a broader console gap: they want a workflow that lets them compare cost and latency orthogonally for a tenant (e.g., compare high-cost, low-latency calls vs high-latency, low-cost calls) and pivot quickly to traces and token-paths. Current console tiles mix tenant averages and route slices in ways that hide these relationships.

Proposal (sketch attached):
- A compact "orthogonal inspector" that shows a 2x2 view (cost per call vs p95 latency) per-tenant, with quick links to: token-path heatmap, sample traces, and recent SLO breaches.
- Drillflow that preserves the tenant context (so operations can go from high-cost quadrant -> top token sequences -> trace playback).
- Lightweight export for billing teams so cost attributions are taggable to product lines.

Asks:
1) Product: prioritize whether this is console tile work vs. a playbook feature (roughly 2-3 sprints to prototype).
2) Observability eng: what telemetry/labels are missing to make per-tenant cost attribution reliable?
3) Platform: any gating infra changes (sampling qps, KV cache telemetry) we should flag.

Attachments: orthogonalization-sketch.pdf for a rough mock and a short example flow I ran with Acme's data.

Why this matters: Acme flagged that they can’t triage cost+latency tradeoffs at tenant-level without manual correlation — it’s a blocker for them to move more of their traffic to Dedicated. If we can give them a low-friction investigator experience, it could accelerate conversion and reduce support escalations.

Next step: a 30-minute sync? I'm proposing Thu 4/22 10:00 PT — can everyone make it?

Thanks,
Elliot
Elliot Price
Senior Product Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>, Observability Eng <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Platform Eng Lead <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Acme Analytics <amanda@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant orthogonalization — cost & latency workflow

Elliot — thanks for the clear ask and mock. I like the 2x2 orthogonal view idea. A few clarifying Qs before we lock in scope for a prototype: 

1) Highest-value scenarios: is the primary goal investigative (for SRE/CS/ops) or for product owners to reassign cost? We should explicitly list use-cases so we design the export/filters correctly.
2) Sampling constraints: do we expect full trace capture for every tenant or a guided sampling approach? Guided sampling will change both UI expectations and infra work.
3) SLO alignment: are we mapping p95/p99 to tenant SLA buckets? If yes, we need a small SLO registry mapping for the MVP.

For the prototype I propose an MVP that focuses on investigative flows (SRE/CS) only:
- Orthogonal tile (tenant-scoped) with links to 10 sample traces and top-10 token sequences.
- Cost attribution that uses existing token-path heuristics (with a clear caveat).
- Manual export button for billing CSVs.

Irene — can you confirm what labels we absolutely need and whether JIRA-OBS-1427 (instrumentation backlog) covers them? If not, can you estimate the ETA for gaps?

Thu 4/22 10:00 PT works for me for a quick sync — happy to own the product spec if we align.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>
Cc: Platform Eng Lead <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Acme Analytics <amanda@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant orthogonalization — cost & latency workflow

Thanks for the context — a few technical points we should surface up front so expectations are correct:

- Current telemetry: we have per-request labels: tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, top_k_tokens (sampled). Cost attribution today relies on token-path heuristics that map token ops to billing buckets; that mapping is incomplete for streaming & tool-calling flows.
- Missing pieces: we need (a) a deterministic token-path fingerprint that survives batching/quantization; (b) request-level cost estimation at the time of service (not post-hoc); (c) consistent tenant->product line tags for customer-managed tagging. Those require minor runtime changes and a short schema addition to our trace envelope.
- Instrumentation effort: I estimate 3 weeks for a small runtime change + 2 weeks of e2e validation (sampled jobs) — that maps to JIRA-OBS-1427 but we need to split it into two tickets (runtime change + validation).

Operational constraints: adding request-level cost estimation will increase labeling and storage by ~8% (rough calc) — we should flag this to infra/cost owners. Also, for high-throughput tenants we need to limit trace retention or increase sampling.

Proposed next steps before the sync:
1) I'll attach a short CSV with example gaps from Acme's dataset (attached: cost-mapping.csv).
2) We create two JIRA tasks: OBS-1427-runtime, OBS-1427-validation.
3) Product team to confirm the exact export fields for billing.

I can join Thu 4/22 10:00 PT — will have a brief tech slide ready.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Observability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Kim is assigning this to Vivek to do an initial feasibility spike and to validate the storage/ingest cost delta. Vivek — can you scope a 2-sprint prototype (tech spike + minimal UI prototype) and report back with blockers? If we see heavy infra impact we will pivot to a guided sampling MVP.

I'll also loop in billing ownership after the sync so we can align export needs.

Agree Thu 4/22 10:00 PT — see you then.
